title: Max Verstappen learns GT stewards 'fault' verdict over 'avoidable collision'
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has been handed a reprimand and a behaviour warning point following a first-lap collision during opening practice for the GT World Challenge Europe round at Portimão.

The four-time F1 champion was only a few corners into his first timed lap when he tried to pass Ezequiel Pérez Companc's number 25 Audi at Turn 3.

Verstappen went for the inside line, but there was not enough room between the two cars. Contact followed, and Pérez Companc was sent spinning.

The Red Bull driver was heard venting his frustration over the radio from inside the cockpit in the immediate aftermath.

Stewards hand down verdict

The GTWCE stewards reviewed the incident and opted for a reprimand plus a single behaviour warning point rather than a harsher sanction. Three points trigger an automatic five-place grid penalty.

"The stewards reviewed the video evidence and heard from the drivers of car 3 and car 25," the stewards said in a statement.

"The driver of car 25 stated that he was focused on the cars in front of him and could not see car 3 on his right. He considered the incident to be an unfortunate racing incident.

"The driver of car 3 explained that he was attempting to pass, expecting car 25 to stay on the outside of the turn. He was surprised when car 25 turned in.

"After thoroughly reviewing the case, the stewards concluded that car 3 had caused an avoidable collision with car 25 at Turn 3 and was entirely at fault for the incident."

Despite placing full blame on Verstappen, the stewards pointed to mitigating circumstances for their choice of penalty.

"The incident took place on the first lap of the first free practice session, and the line of cars in front of car 25 affected the line that car 25 could take," the statement added. "Therefore, the stewards decided to impose the penalty mentioned above."

title: F1 veteran confirmed as Lola Formula E deputy team principal
excerpt:
Lola has appointed Gerry Hughes as deputy team principal, bringing the Formula E and Formula 1 veteran back into the fold as the team prepares to enter the Gen4 era from its new Silverstone headquarters.

Hughes will take charge of all operations and sporting matters for the team, overseeing its day-to-day running as it builds on the progress made across its first two seasons.

The appointment represents something of a homecoming. Hughes previously served as Lola's Head of F1 Engineering back in 2009, and his connection to the marque stretches back even further, having carried out his MSc research thesis on suspension design with the company while studying automotive engineering at Cranfield University.

His career since has taken in touring cars and F1 as a race engineer, before a move into Formula E that eventually saw him rise to team principal at NIO.

Lola and Hughes reunited again

Team principal Mark Preston said the experience Hughes brings will be central to Lola's plans heading into the new Gen4 regulations.

"We are very pleased to announce that Gerry is joining the team," Preston said.

"His vast experience across a variety of motorsport series will be integral to the team's continued development as we enter GEN4.

"On a personal note, it's great to be working with Gerry again having been teammates at Super Aguri as well as competitors in the earlier seasons of Formula E. This appointment continues our commitment to building a competitive in-house team with wide-ranging expertise and capabilities."

Hughes, for his part, described the move as a proud moment, and one that reunites him with familiar faces.

"Having worked for Lola on two previous occasions, the opportunity to re-join the prestigious British marque is something of a homecoming for me and one that I take great pride in," Hughes said.

"Joining Lola also marks the third time I have worked alongside Mark Preston and Peter McCool, so there are a number of familiarities which will help me hit the ground running.

"Formula E has certainly come a long way technologically since I bowed out at the end of Season 5 and I am excited to be returning to the championship as it enters this new era."

The news comes alongside confirmation that the squad will race simply as the Lola Formula E Team next season, with Yamaha continuing as technical partner.

title: Ollie Bearman F1 contract delay explained after Haas sign new driver
excerpt:
Haas has confirmed Rafael Camara will drive for the team in 2027, but so far, Ollie Bearman is still waiting to know his future.

Haas may have confirmed Rafael Camara as one of its drivers for 2027, but it has still not formally announced that Oliver Bearman will remain alongside him.

The team announced on Wednesday that Camara, the reigning FIA Formula 3 champion and a Ferrari Driver Academy member, has signed a multi-year deal to replace Esteban Ocon from next season.

Camara impressed Haas during a private Testing of Previous Cars evaluation at Portimao in August, having already claimed back-to-back junior titles with the 2024 Formula Regional European Championship and last year's F3 crown. He currently leads the F2 standings.

Bearman's side of the 2027 line-up, however, remains unconfirmed in public terms, despite the Briton having signed a multi-year agreement with Haas back in July 2024 that is understood to cover the 2025 and 2026 seasons, and with an option for next year.

Speculation over an early promotion to Ferrari for 2027 has also faded, with the Scuderia having locked in Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton for the long term, closing off any seat at Maranello.

Haas move to reassure

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu addressed the uncertainty when speaking to the media, including RacingNews365, insisting the delay is procedural rather than a sign of doubt over Bearman's future.

"For me, I'd like to continue with Ollie. He's an incredible talent who has shown amazing growth, and this year he's shown he's ready to be a team leader, and then you all saw how he raced in Singapore, which was very impressive.

title: Red Bull hit limit but send ominous warning to F1 rivals: 'Don't get me wrong'
excerpt:
Red Bull boss Laurent Mekies is adamant that despite the team having no further substantial upgrades to come this season, the Milton Keynes-based squad will not stop trying to improve.

Red Bull will introduce no further major upgrades to the RB22 this F1 season, team principal Laurent Mekies has confirmed, as the Milton Keynes outfit shifts its full development focus onto 2027.

Despite freezing further substantial updates to the current car, Mekies, whose contract Red Bull has recently extended until 2031, was adamant that the team's pursuit of performance will not slow down.

The Frenchman was clear that — having achieved the primary aim of winning a grand prix this season, courtesy of Max Verstappen in Sepang and Singapore — the team was focused on its target of taking all the lessons it can into next year.

"So there will be no other substantial upgrades to the car," Mekies told media, including RacingNews365.

"Now, don't get me wrong; it does not mean that we will not continue to push very hard to improve. Continue to push very hard to use every remaining race to learn for this year and to learn for next year.

"That's what we had said to each other: 'The first win is the target, but the other target is to take all the learning.

"So the development programme will not change. We have put our focus on '27. We think there is still a huge amount of learning in '26 that we could use in '27."

[Article continues below]

Praise for Waché and Hodgkinson

Verstappen swept both pole position and victory in both races at the Singapore Grand Prix last weekend.

Mekies used the result to praise the technical departments behind the RB22's chassis and its Red Bull-Ford power unit, led respectively by Pierre Waché and Ben Hodgkinson.

However, he insists the team remains far from satisfied, a sentiment very much in step with the desire to keep learning across the remainder of the current campaign.

"I'd like to take the time to say a huge congrats to Pierre's [Waché] team, to Ben's [Hodgkinson] team, for the 360-degree work they have done in order to be in that position to fight for wins on different tracks," Mekies added.

"As I said, even on a weekend where you take two poles and two wins like [in Singapore], we are still very honest with each other about the fact that there were still a number of things we would like to see done better, even on a weekend like this.

"And that's the spirit of this team, and it's with that spirit that we will go on and reset and tackle the next races."

Max Verstappen is facing a stewards' investigation after a clash with an Audi during opening practice for the GTWCE round at Portimão.

The four-time Formula 1 champion was back behind the wheel of the Mercedes-AMG GT3, after already turning laps on Thursday's paid test session. Free Practice 1 got underway at 08:45 BST on the Algarve circuit, marking the first official session of the weekend.

Verstappen wasted no time getting out on track in the #3 car, settling in for what would become a lengthy stint. But before it really got going, there was early drama in Turn 3, where he attempted to pass the #25 Audi of Ezequiel Pérez Companc on the inside.

There was not enough room for the move, and the Audi was sent into a spin. The incident is now being looked at by race control.

Max Verstappen gathers significant data

Verstappen stayed out for 27 laps, racking up more than 40 minutes of track time during the 90-minute session.

His pace improved steadily throughout the run, climbing from the higher 1m 43s bracket early on to a best lap of 1m 43.046, which was good enough for 18th at the time, in a field of 61 cars where the gaps at the front were tiny.

After his stint, Verstappen handed the car over to team-mate Chris Lulham, the only full-time Verstappen Racing driver on duty this weekend. The Briton used his laps to build up rhythm but could not beat Verstappen's time.

Ben Barnicoat then took his turn behind the wheel but also failed to improve on the benchmark, leaving the team in 20th place overall.

It was a German affair at the top of the times, with Marcus Winkelhock quickest in the #84 Audi R8 LMS GT3 on a 1m42.643. He was followed by the #32 BMW, the #99 Audi, the #98 BMW and the #46 BMW, the latter featuring Valentino Rossi among its drivers.

The best-placed Mercedes was the #17 Team GetSpeed entry in sixth, meaning Verstappen's squad ended up around four tenths off the pace. The times carry little weight at this stage of the weekend, however, with the focus still on fine-tuning the car's set-up ahead of qualifying and the race.

title: Ferrari confirm two driver academy departures as fresh plans revealed
excerpt:
Ferrari has confirmed who will be part of its driver academy for 2027.

Ferrari has confirmed that Dino Beganovic and Rafael Camara have graduated out of the Scuderia's driver academy, as the Maranello outfit unveiled its 2027 junior line-up featuring three new recruits.

Camara will step up to Formula 1 with Haas next year, while Beganovic stays on at Ferrari as a development and reserve driver, sharing those duties with Antonio Giovinazzi.

The Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy will field eight drivers across karting, F4, Formula Regional, F3, F2 and F1 Academy in 2027.

Three newcomers join the roster: Turkish driver Alp Aksoy, Colombian Salim Hanna and Dutchman Daniel Miron.

Ferrari reveal 2027 driver academy line-up

Miron, the youngest of the new arrivals at just 13, moves up to the OK karting class after finishing runner-up in the European FIA Championship's OK-Junior category in 2026.

Noah Baglin and Filippo Sala make the leap from karting to single-seaters, both racing in Spanish F4 next year. Baglin arrives as reigning European OK champion and Junior World champion, while Sala impressed across the European Championship and Champions of the Future series.

Aksoy steps up to the European Formula Regional Championship after a strong rookie single-seater campaign that yielded three wins in Italian F4 and the Euro4 series.

Alba Larsen continues in F1 Academy for a second year, having claimed back-to-back podiums at Zandvoort in her debut campaign.

Hanna moves into a full Formula 3 season after winning at Imola in Formula Regional this year, joined by Niccolò Maccagnani, who steps up from F4 after victories at Misano and Mugello.

Tuukka Taponen completes the roster with a move to Formula 2 with ART Grand Prix, the team he raced with in his first F3 season in 2025. The Finn finished third in this year's F3 standings with a win and two further podiums.
